extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying or evaluating behavioral/lifestyle obesity interventions (systematic reviewers, intervention designers, health behaviour scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review guidance and empirical criteria for identifying and judging individual-level mediators/predictors of weight, physical activity, and dietary outcomes in lifestyle obesity interventions for adults. Emphasizes methodological and analytic features that affect causal inference about mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness (selection bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether study samples are representative of the target population (selection bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the review studies were rated weak/moderate/strong on Representativeness; most studies scored moderate. Representativeness is a component of the quality assessment (EPHPP-adapted) and contributes to the global methodological quality rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of withdrawals and dropouts
rubrics_metrics.description: How well studies report participant withdrawals and dropouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated weak/moderate/strong; in this review 5 studies were weak, 16 moderate, 14 strong. Clear reporting of attrition is required to judge bias and interpret effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for confounders in analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether analyses adjusted for relevant confounding variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated weak/moderate/strong; adjustment for confounders affects the credibility of mediation/predictor findings. In the review 4 studies were weak, 10 moderate, 21 strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection tools: validity and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether measurement instruments' validity and reliability (psychometric properties) are reported or established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated weak/moderate/strong; absence of information on validity/reliability leads to weak rating. Some studies using larger datasets were not rated because psychometric properties were provided elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of suitable statistical methods for the study questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All included studies scored strong on use of appropriate statistical analyses in this review. Appropriate analyses are necessary but do not by themselves guarantee strong causal inference for mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall reporting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Completeness and transparency of study reporting (methods, measures, analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated (in this review) as strong or moderate; 30 studies were strong and 5 moderate. Good reporting aids interpretation of mediation analyses and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global methodological quality (EPHPP-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite/overall study quality rating (e.g., weak/moderate/strong) based on multiple domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify studies; in this review very few studies were globally weak and none of the studies with formal mediation analysis were classified as strong on methodological quality. Global quality should be considered when interpreting mediator/predictor findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal mediation analysis (vs correlational/non-formal analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mediation was tested using formal statistical mediation methods (preferred) rather than relying on correlational/non-formal tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review gives special emphasis to variables tested as formal mediators, stating that formal mediation analyses 'provide the best possible inferences regarding causal determinants of behavior change.' Many reported effects, however, were based on correlational analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot studies to test mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether authors conducted pilot studies specifically to test mediation prior to main studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the reviewed studies reported conducting pilot studies to test mediation. The presence of pilot mediation work is considered desirable for planning and assessing feasibility/power of mediation tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to detect mediation (mediation-specific power analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether studies report power calculations or other information indicating adequate sample size to detect mediation effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the review, almost all studies lacked specific information regarding power to detect mediation; reporting/consideration of mediation power is recommended because many mediation effects require larger samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlling outcomes for baseline values
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mediation/outcome analyses control for baseline values of the outcome (or mediator) to increase rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only six studies in the review controlled outcomes for baseline values. Controlling baseline values is noted as an important analytic step in mediation evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized controlled trial design (RCT status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the study is an RCT, which strengthens causal inference for mediation when combined with formal mediation tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several of the long-term mediation findings came from RCTs that included formal mediation tests; RCTs with mediation analysis provide stronger evidence for causal mediators than non-randomized designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multivariate analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for multivariate analyses (adjusting for covariates) over simple correlations when inferring mediation or predictor effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results from multivariate analyses were given more weight; self-regulation skill use showed consistent effects especially in multivariate analyses. Correlational findings are considered weaker evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and frequency of effects (vote-counting/percent times tested)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a variable shows effects across the number of times it was tested (e.g., percentage of tests showing an effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review organized results by 'times tested' and reported 'Effect, %' (percentage of tests showing an effect). It used vote counting of statistically significant mediation effects to indicate whether a variable can be identified as a mediator, while acknowledging this method's limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on statistical significance to infer mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Using statistical significance of mediation parameters as the primary criterion to claim mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review notes that in primary studies the statistical significance of mediation effects was typically used to infer mediation; this approach has limitations and is affected by power and multiple testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity of studies (designs/measures/interventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of heterogeneity across studies in designs, measures, intervention formats, populations, and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large heterogeneity precluded pooling mediation effects in meta-analysis and complicates synthesis. Homogeneity in measures and clearer intervention descriptions would facilitate stronger synthesis and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of validated and standardized outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (and reporting) of validated, standardized measures for outcomes and mediators to improve comparability and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review highlights variability in measures (especially for physical activity) as a limitation and recommends using validated instruments and reporting psychometric properties to aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: External validity and generalizability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether findings are generalizable across populations and settings, including dependence on a small number of research groups or similar study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review cautions that findings (e.g., for self-regulation skills and autonomous motivation) may have limited external validity because they derive from few studies by a small number of groups using similar designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for detailed reporting of intervention content and targeted self-regulation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether studies describe intervention content and the specific self-regulation factors addressed, to allow interpretation of mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review recommends that future studies provide more detail on intervention content and the self-regulation factors targeted to facilitate interpretation of mediation results and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses to account for study quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct sensitivity analyses to examine whether results depend on methodological quality or other study characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors suggest future reviews would benefit from sensitivity analyses because some mediator findings were concentrated in poorer-quality studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability: targeting identified mediators in interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate mediator evidence into practice by incorporating behavior change techniques that specifically target promising mediators (e.g., self-efficacy, autonomous motivation, self-regulation skills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review recommends integrating techniques known to change identified mediators into future interventions and training health professionals to assess and target these variables (e.g., brief questionnaires, motivational interviewing techniques).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-frame categorization (short-term vs long-term outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and separate consideration of short-term and long-term outcomes when evaluating mediators (e.g., short-term <12 months for weight; short-term <6 months for physical activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review analyzed mediators separately for short-term and long-term outcomes and reports that some mediators are more consistent in the short-term than long-term. Time-frame matters for interpreting mediator consistency.
